decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The paper explicitly states in the Introduction (lines 184-188, 220-224) and Discussion (lines 438-457, 481) that the two studies by Ellenbogen et al. (2006 [8] and 2009 [9]) form the basis of the present replication testing whether sleep protects declarative word-pair memories against retroactive A-C interference learning, and directly compares its null Sleep x Interference interaction against both the 2006 and 2009 findings. Reference 8 (line 533) verifies the identity of Ellenbogen et al. (2006) in Current Biology (16: 1290-1294). The sole shipped row (input_row_index 309, Ellenbogen et al., 2009, 10.1371/journal.pone.0004117, matched to sibling target_index 1) is a separate follow-up experiment with a within-subjects design rather than the 2006 between-subjects experiment, and sibling target_index 2 (Tucker et al., 2018) is an unrelated study on intrinsic motivation; thus report equivalence does not apply and target_index 0 is genuinely absent.
